output.question: What are Restaurant Brands International's subsidiaries?
output.answer: As of its Q3 2026 results on October 29, 2026, Restaurant Brands International (RBI) owns four restaurant brands: Tim Hortons, Burger King, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs. It operates in more than 120 countries and territories, with over 33,000 restaurants and over $49 billion in annual system-wide sales. RBI also owns restaurants directly through its Restaurant Holdings (RH) segment, which holds the Carrols Burger King restaurants, Popeyes China and Firehouse Subs Brazil. RBI plans to wind that segment down by refranchising the Carrols restaurants and finding new investors for Popeyes China and Firehouse Subs Brazil. Burger King China is no longer fully owned: on January 30, 2026, RBI formed a joint venture with CPE, stopped consolidating BK China in its accounts, and now holds a 17% equity stake.

key_facts.fact: RBI owns four brands: Tim Hortons, Burger King, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs.
RBI has over $49 billion in annual system-wide sales and over 33,000 restaurants in more than 120 countries and territories.

RBI's Restaurant Holdings (RH) segment includes the Carrols Burger King restaurants, Popeyes China (PLK China) and Firehouse Subs Brazil. RBI plans to refranchise most of the Carrols restaurants, find new investors for PLK China and FHS Brazil, and then close the segment.
On January 30, 2026, RBI formed a Burger King China joint venture with CPE Alder Investment Limited, which invested $350 million. RBI deconsolidated BK China and now holds a 17% equity interest.
RBI reports six segments: TH, BK, PLK and FHS (the U.S. and Canada franchisors for each brand), INTL (all brands in the rest of the world) and RH.

caveats: The brand list and segment details come from a summary of the Q3 2026 press release as republished on Finviz. Only the first 'About' sentence is quoted word for word; the rest is paraphrased.

This answer covers brands and business segments, not the full list of legal entities. That list, including holding entities such as Restaurant Brands International Limited Partnership, is in Exhibit 21 of the 10-K, which I did not open.
Burger King China is now a 17% equity-method investment and no longer a consolidated subsidiary.
The Restaurant Holdings segment, which includes Carrols, Popeyes China and Firehouse Subs Brazil, is being wound down, so ownership of these businesses may change.
